summary.text:
Global equities suffered a broad sell-off led by tech, with the Nasdaq dropping 5.47% to 25065.4023 and the S&P 500 down 3.59% to 6918.4502 as volatility surged, lifting the VIX 27.36% to 36.22. Technology shares were pressured by Nvidia plunging 13.83% to 125.79 and news that Donald Trump threatened taxes and bans on US companies building artificial intelligence data centers overseas.

In currencies, the dollar index was little changed at 103.889, with EURUSD at 1.0966 and USDJPY sliding 0.5% to 158.589. Commodities saw gold tumble 4.57% to 3517.1001. Energy markets were mixed, with WTI crude up 0.59% to 83.7 while Brent fell 2.17% to 89.98. Bitcoin declined 5.34% to 58596.7109.

Looking ahead, market participants should watch ongoing Federal Reserve official commentary and political developments regarding international data center restrictions. Attention also centers on potential cybersecurity consolidation following reports that CrowdStrike is in talks to acquire Zscaler.
